headline: Highest risk is medium data leakage: Perplexity uploads files and browses vendor-side while Botpress can ingest content, but no shared filesystem or direct injection channel is documented.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Botpress is a customer-support agent with no documented shared channel to Perplexity, while Perplexity can browse and analyze uploaded documents. The pair lacks a proven direct ingestion bridge, so prompt injection is only plausible through manual copy-paste or user-mediated transfer, which keeps blast radius small.
conditions: IF the operator copies Perplexity-generated text into Botpress prompts without sanitization, injection becomes plausible.
IF a shared workspace or connector is added later, the risk increases.
mitigations: Strip instructions from copied text before pasting.
Use a fixed prompt template in Botpress.
Disable any future shared connector unless reviewed.
Mark Perplexity outputs as untrusted in operator SOP.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Perplexity touches uploaded documents and browsing context and sends queries to vendor APIs, while Botpress has no documented filesystem or network egress surface in this profile. The pair can leak sensitive content if the operator feeds the same documents into Perplexity and then reuses outputs in Botpress; this is a default-use pathway, though not a guaranteed cross-agent exfiltration channel.
conditions: IF sensitive documents are uploaded to Perplexity and then summarized into Botpress workflows, leakage risk exists.
IF Botpress is later connected to a shared workspace, the blast radius expands.
mitigations: Avoid uploading secrets or regulated data to Perplexity.
Redact documents before analysis.
Keep Botpress and Perplexity on separate workspaces.
Review Perplexity privacy settings before use.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Botpress can install packages, but Perplexity cannot write the filesystem, modify git state, or execute shell commands. There is no overlapping write surface or shared mutable resource documented, so direct capability conflict is limited to read-only coordination issues rather than destructive contention.
conditions: IF both agents are later granted write access to the same directory, conflict risk rises.
IF an orchestrator adds shared mutable state, contention becomes possible.
mitigations: Keep each agent in separate directories.
Do not grant Botpress shared write access.
Avoid using Perplexity as a file editor.
Add a manual handoff step for any mutable artifact.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Perplexity is explicitly a citation-producing answer engine, and Botpress is a customer-support agent that may operationalize outputs. If Botpress treats Perplexity answers as authoritative without verification, errors can cascade into incorrect support actions or messages. The interaction is inferred from documented roles, not directly sandboxed, so uncertainty stays above low.
conditions: IF Botpress forwards Perplexity answers to end users without review, cascading error occurs.
IF Botpress adds automated action-taking based on Perplexity output, impact increases.
mitigations: Require human review before sending support replies.
Add a verification checklist for cited facts.
Limit Perplexity to draft generation only.
Log source links alongside every answer.

E_compliance.rationale: Perplexity is vendor-hosted and processes search queries, uploaded documents, and browsing context, while Botpress is open-source with no documented residency or retention controls in this profile. If regulated data is routed through Perplexity, compliance obligations may differ from Botpress deployments; the mismatch is plausible but not specifically documented for this pair.
conditions: IF EU personal data or regulated records are uploaded to Perplexity, residency and retention review is required.
IF Botpress is deployed under stricter local policy than Perplexity, mismatch becomes material.
mitigations: Classify data before sending it to Perplexity.
Confirm retention settings in Perplexity admin controls.
Keep regulated data out of vendor-hosted workflows.
Document a data-processing review for the pair.
